title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous and next pages): X and Y are smooth projective connected varieties over an algebraically closed field k, with X of dimension n and Y of dimension m. A_T is the Albanese variety of T and B_T = Pic^0_T is its Picard variety. Cohomology is ℓ-adic with Q_ℓ coefficients. There are canonical isomorphisms φ_T : H^1(A_T) → H^1(T), from pullback along the Albanese map, and ψ_T : H^{2d-1}(T)(d-1) → H^1(B_T), with d = dim T; the latter combines Poincaré duality with the duality between Alb and Pic^0.

The page classifies the four ways a correspondence can act on the 'degree-one part' of cohomology. Each type matches a kind of homomorphism of abelian varieties and an algebraic cycle on X×Y of a definite dimension.

(I) Y → X on H^1 → H^1. This matches homomorphisms A_X → A_Y, given by cycles of dimension m (codimension n) on X×Y. The next page's Th. 1.1 constructs u_Z : A_Y → A_X functorially in Z, depending only on the numerical class of Z.

(II) The transposed case, H^{2m-1}(Y)(m-1) → H^{2n-1}(X). This matches homomorphisms B_X → B_Y. 'Cas transposés l'un de l'autre': transposing Z swaps the two cases, compatibly with dual isogenies.

(III) H^{2m-1}(Y)(m-1) → H^1(X). This matches B_Y ← A_X, i.e. homomorphisms Alb_X → Pic^0_Y. The relevant cycles are divisor classes on X×Y, the Künneth component in H^1⊗H^1 ⊂ H^2. The case is self-transposed. Here every homomorphism comes from a cycle with integral coefficients: pull back the Poincaré-type line bundle on A_X × Y. This is the classical theory of divisorial correspondences (Weil, Matsusaka, Lang).

(IV) H^1(Y) → H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1). This matches B_X → A_Y, i.e. Pic^0_X → Alb_Y, realized by 1-cycles on X×Y. It is also self-transposed.

The question being addressed is the converse of Th. 1.1, a 'Hodge/Tate for degree-one Künneth components' statement: is every homomorphism of abelian varieties, viewed as a map of H^1, induced by an algebraic cycle on X×Y?
- Case III: yes, integrally.
- Case IV: one must make φ_Y^{-1} and ψ_X^{-1} algebraic, which introduces denominators. ψ_X is inverted by the Lefschetz theorem: the hard Lefschetz map H^1 → H^{2n-1} by cup with ξ^{n-1} induces an isogeny Pic^0 → Alb, whose inverse is algebraic with Q-coefficients.
- Cases I and II: one needs to invert φ_Y, respectively φ_X (or ψ). The marginal note 'il faut des dénominateurs ?' records uncertainty about whether denominators are needed.

The last lines say how to invert φ_X: use Lefschetz plus the special case of abelian varieties themselves. The net conclusion is that all degree-one correspondences are Q-algebraic, i.e. the Hodge/Tate and Lefschetz-type standard conjectures hold for the H^1⊗H^1 Künneth part. This is a preparatory step in the 1965–71 notes on the standard conjectures.
errors: The marginal question 'il faut des dénominateurs ?' for cases I/II is left open on the page. In fact Q-coefficients suffice; integrality fails in general, e.g. one cannot always realize an isogeny's inverse integrally.
The labelling of which map must be inverted in case II is ambiguous in the handwriting (φ_X vs ψ_X). By transposition with case I it should involve ψ, or φ applied to the transposed correspondence.
No proof is given on this page; it is a schematic plan.

ideas.what: Classification of degree-one correspondences into four types (H^1→H^1, H^{2m-1}→H^{2n-1}, H^{2m-1}→H^1, H^1→H^{2n-1}), matching Hom(A_X,A_Y), Hom(B_X,B_Y), Hom(A_X,B_Y), Hom(B_X,A_Y), with transposition symmetry
ideas.modern_name: Degree-one part of the Chow motive (h^1 and h^{2d-1}) and its identification with the isogeny category of abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (correspondences), Matsusaka, Lang; motivic formulation by Grothendieck/Manin/Kleiman (1968), Murre (Picard and Albanese motives, 1990)
ideas.where_published: Ideas present in Grothendieck's 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) and in Kleiman's 1968 exposé, not in this tabular form

ideas.what: Divisorial correspondences: every homomorphism Alb_X → Pic^0_Y comes from a divisor on X×Y, integrally
ideas.where_published: Classical; implicitly in FGA/Picard scheme discussions

ideas.what: Using hard Lefschetz on H^1 (the isogeny Pic^0 → Alb from ξ^{n-1}) to show inverses are Q-algebraic, so degree-one Künneth classes are algebraic
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture B in degree 1 / algebraicity of H^1 Künneth components

deep.surprise_reason: A schematic table organizing classical facts: Weil–Lang divisorial correspondences, and the Q-algebraicity of H^1 correspondences via Lefschetz. These were published in the standard-conjecture literature (Grothendieck 1969, Kleiman 1968). Nothing here appears absent from the record.
transcription_corrections: 'des lieux de VA' is more plausibly 'des hom[omorphismes] de VA' (homomorphisms of abelian varieties).
In case IV the target should be H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1), since dim X = n; the page writes indices m loosely.
Case I reads 'il faut inverser φ_Y' (possibly 'il faudrait'). Right margin: '— φ_X } il faut des dénominateurs ?' applies to case II, whose struck text is '[Cas pareil]'.
Final line ending 'qui est linéaire' is uncertain; possibly 'qu'on a traité' or similar.
